title: Spec amendment: the dispatch posture split (attended/autonomous), from mdatron's kickoff live fire
description: Directive classification, recorded before execution per Directive reconciliation: the operator relayed mdatron's kickoff live-fire field report (three fix-lane agents dispatched local/tmux, unattended, idled to timeout with zero tracker activity; post-mortem names the attended/autonomous posture axis the dispatch contract does not model) with direction to address it as part of the design. Classification: SPEC AMENDMENT touching Recorded review dispatch (posture axis, manifest posture recording, launch derivation), Gates (never-started as a distinct loud state; dispatch preflight), Trust boundaries (consent provisioning is an operator setup act — the orchestrator never provisions autonomy for its sub-agents; identity pre-approval before launch), the data-authoring package (posture enumeration), and Decomposition routing (Layer 0 substrate setup items; Layer 8 preflight and derivation). Served by: the chassis-managed spec-review loop, folded into the open phase-1c review cycle as a declared concurrent scope. Ratification: operator-gated, per the standing loop. Evidence: mdatron's report of 2026-07-20 (relayed image), its three dead-agent post-mortem and the orchestrator-consent-refusal observation.

Dispatch manifest — round 4 amendment lenses: solution-architect and ai-engineer, cold, fresh readers; declared narrowing: no UX lens (no human-facing surface beyond diagnostics) and no SE lens (spec-stage, no code mechanics beyond SA's reach) — reasons recorded here per loop practice. comments.author: xqjG
comments.content: Operator-directed deep dive into crosslink and Thermite completed before redraft (two very thorough parallel cold reads; full synthesis on the knowledge page 'attended-design-autonomous-execution'). Both repos implement the operator's structural ruling literally: crosslink's /design is conversational-attended by construction (no source edits, no auto-dispatch, wait-for-user) while kickoff/swarm are the autonomous executors, with the human as 'driver' acting between runs — trust attach, gates, checkpoints, merges, sentinel triage; Thermite activates autonomy by explicit human act (/goal) bounded by a mechanical stop condition, with named human-required slots (pushes, design amendments, oracle authorship, stage gates, waiver review, spec-intent review) and the do-not-re-litigate register pattern freezing attended decisions against autonomous reopening. Redraft-shaping findings: (1) never-started classification upstream is launch-status sentinel + session records + heartbeat staleness, NOT tracker-event counting — resolving the round-4 reviewer objection; (2) crosslink's trust move 'the driver explicitly invoked kickoff, so trust is implicit' grounds consent-as-dispatch-act; (3) preflight checks should carry three-valued honesty (pass/fail/INCONCLUSIVE, fail-closed); (4) escalate-don't-guess conduct for unresolved questions reaching autonomous runs; (5) three doc-vs-code mismatches in crosslink logged as upstream findings (agent_overrides vs no-push-no-merge docs; container-run missing skip-permissions; TIMEOUT sentinel never written). Redraft remains held for operator go.

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content: Operator raised the chassis-affordance gap; install audit of vsdd-cli run in response. Findings: (1) .claude/settings.json wires every crosslink hook through guard shims (if [ -f HOOK ]) but .claude/hooks/ does not exist — the entire enforcement layer silently no-ops; (2) .mcp.json wires the three crosslink MCP servers (agent-prompt, knowledge, safe-fetch) at .claude/mcp/*.py which does not exist — dangling, with enableAllProjectMcpServers: true set; (3) .claude/commands/ carries only the vsdd primers and domain prompts — none of crosslink's fourteen skills (design, kickoff, check, commit, review, workflow, preflight, qa, ...) are installed, so no keyword or description match could ever summon them; (4) .crosslink/rules/ is fully populated but its injector (prompt-guard) is among the absent hooks, so the rules content is never injected. The estate's chassis install is a hollow shell that fails open by the guard-shim design — the silent-degradation class the contract's never-silent and three-valued disciplines exist to kill, in our own substrate. Structural-closure proposal drafted for operator review; no contract authoring until the operator rules.

Inherited model at session effort. Falsifier: clean-while-defective falsifies; citations required; stop signal: clean or hallucinated-only.

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content: CORRECTION and new finding, from the operator's restart attempt. Claude Code keys conversations AND project config to the launch directory. This estate's sessions have always launched from the workspace root (not a git repo, no chassis config beyond the statusline) — so: (1) 'claude --continue' from vsdd-cli found no session, correctly — the conversation lives in the root-keyed project; (2) more important, vsdd-cli's .claude/settings.json hooks, .mcp.json servers, and command listing DO NOT LOAD into root-launched sessions at all — the repaired substrate binds only to sessions launched from the repo directory. My earlier result comment's claim that work-check 'armed mid-session' was wrong: I verified the hook scripts execute by invoking them directly, but this session's harness wiring comes from the root settings, which carry only the statusline — no hook has ever fired in these sessions. The repair is real and banked: the operator's trust approval during the restart attempt bound to the vsdd-cli project path (persistent), uv is installed, payloads are complete — a session launched from vsdd-cli gets the full armed substrate. New structural finding for the amendment: the estate's workspace-root session shape is off-chassis — crosslink assumes repo-rooted sessions, and the session-split ruling already points the same direction; the session-shape rule (repo-rooted sessions; workspace root for cross-repo orchestration only) is an operator decision to fold into the affordance closure.
